transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… mostly my wife’s been noticing I don’t seem to take things in. She’ll be telling me about my cousin’s appointments or rides, and I’ll be looking right at her, but a minute later I realize I missed half of what she said.
When someone tells you something important, do you usually remember it later if you make a point to focus on it?

I mean, I try to focus, yeah. But even then… like with my wife telling me about my cousin’s appointments or rides, I can be looking right at her, and a minute later I realize I didn’t really take in half of it.
Have you had this kind of trouble paying attention since you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. Back in grade school, before I was 12, teachers used to tell my parents I was bright, but that I’d be daydreaming a lot. I’d leave homework in my desk, that kind of thing… and needed reminders to finish classwork.
Do these attention problems also happen at work?

I’m not really working now, but when I do catering-type jobs, yeah… I have to double-check myself or sometimes redo little things so orders or small tasks don’t get mixed up. It’s more noticeable at home lately, though. My wife gets frustrated because she feels like she can’t count on me with my cousin’s care.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Not really… I mean, I get frustrated sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling depressed.
Do you often feel anxious or worried?
Not really. I mean, I worry about normal stuff, I guess, but I wouldn’t say I’m anxious all the time.
Have these attention problems been about the same throughout your life, rather than getting clearly worse only recently?

Yeah… I think it’s been there a long time. Even in grade school, before I was 12, teachers would tell my parents I was bright, but I’d be daydreaming or leave homework in my desk. I needed reminders to finish classwork. So it’s not just something that started recently.
